concern_details.detail: How do the components collaborate when invalid or already existing user data is provided?
concern_details.why: The three rejection points are shown in the right order: format checks inside User manager, then the email lookup, then the identifier lookup through User registry and Persistence manager. Each throws IllegalArgumentException, and the error handler maps it to 400, which matches UserManager.java:65-97 and RestExceptionHandler.java:19-22. Several things a tester needs are weak or missing. (a) The save-failure branch has no trigger. In the code, User.institutionalEmail, Student.studentNumber and Librarian.internalIdentifierCode are unique columns, so a duplicate that gets past the lookups (for example, two concurrent registrations) makes PersistenceManager.save roll back and return false. That is the second line of defence against existing data, and the view does not say so. (b) The outcome of that branch is left as 'unconfirmed'. The handler maps only IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException, so the RuntimeException falls through to Spring's default server error (500). This is the response the tester must assert. (c) The identifier lookup is role-scoped: a student number is checked only against students, and a librarian code only against librarians (UserManager.java:81-83). The merged label 'find student or librarian' hides this boundary case. (d) The error return path is drawn only for the first branch; the email and ID branches say '(same path to 400)'.

level_why: Seven lifelines, each one an integration point the tester would stub or observe (controller, facade, manager, registry, persistence, factories, error handler), fits a balanced level. Leaving MySQL, the entities, UserDTO and the Swing form out of the lifelines is a sensible cut. The view does not need more lifelines. What it needs is more precise guards and outcomes inside the existing fragments.
unsupported: 'api --> eh : exception' is drawn as a reply message from Registration API to the REST error handler. The controller never calls or returns to RestExceptionHandler (AuthenticationController.java:22-31). Spring's dispatcher routes the exception to the @RestControllerAdvice, so the message should be shown as framework dispatch, not as a reply from the controller.

The note 'Not mapped by the error handler (outcome unconfirmed)' understates what the code shows. RestExceptionHandler handles only IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException and SecurityException, so the RuntimeException('Server error: the user could not be saved...') from UserManager.java:94 gets the framework default 500 response.

The Swing note is attached to User factories, but the Swing Registration form calls LibraryFacade.register (Registration.java:134) and catches RuntimeException (Registration.java:140). The note belongs on Library facade.
missing: The trigger for the 'failed' save branch: a unique-constraint violation on email, student number or librarian code (User.java:21, Student.java:19, Librarian.java:13), caught by PersistenceManager.save (PersistenceManager.java:31-38), which rolls back and returns false. This is how already existing data is caught when the lookups miss it.
The HTTP outcome of the save-failure branch: the default server error (500), because no handler maps RuntimeException. The view should show it as the response to the found message.

The identifier lookup is role-specific: findStudentByStudentNumber for students and findLibrarianByCode for librarians (UserRegistry.java:44-60). A student number equal to an existing librarian code is not rejected. Splitting the guard or the label (student: by student number / librarian: by code) would expose this test case.

The guard 'format invalid' should list the checks that differ by role. The role must be Student or Librarian (otherwise 'A valid role is required'), only students get the student-ID regex (UserManager.java:177), and anything that is not Student is treated as Librarian after validation. These are the role-specific validation integration cases the request names.
uml: Exceptions are drawn as ordinary reply messages (dashed arrows labelled IllegalArgumentException), and the activations of User manager, Library facade and Registration API are not closed in the error branches, so after an exception the lifelines look like they keep running. Either end the activations in each error operand or use a single reply labelled e.g. 'register(...) : IllegalArgumentException(msg)'.
'api --> eh : exception' is a reply message with no matching call. Draw the error handler as receiving a message from the framework (or a found message) and replying with the 400 response.

The text '(same path to 400)' on a message label stands in for missing interactions. Restructure instead: put the three IllegalArgumentException cases into one operand (or end each operand with the throw) and draw the shared propagation to the error handler once after the combined fragment, or use a ref to a shared interaction.

The lifeline 'User factories' stands for several classes, but a lifeline should represent one participant. Name it e.g. 'factory : UserFactory', with a note saying it is a StudentFactory or LibrarianFactory chosen by role. The create message returns a User, so add a reply or a return value.
fixes: Give the 'failed' save operand a real guard (unique constraint violated, e.g. a concurrent duplicate email or identifier) and end it with the actual HTTP outcome (default 500, since RestExceptionHandler does not map RuntimeException). Replace 'outcome unconfirmed'.

Fix the error propagation notation: drop 'api --> eh' as a reply, show the exception reaching the error handler through framework dispatch, close the activations in the error operands, and replace the '(same path to 400)' labels with one drawn propagation shared by all three rejection cases.

Split the identifier uniqueness exchange by role (student: by student number; librarian: by code) or say in the label that it is role-scoped, so the tester sees that cross-role collisions are not checked.
Make the 'format invalid' guard state the role check (Student or Librarian only) and the student-only ID pattern, so the tests for role-specific validation are visible.
Move the Swing form note to Library facade, and rename 'User factories' to a single typed participant (factory : UserFactory) with a return of the created User.
